experiment: Exp 31 — memory-layer decoding at and beyond the square point (P2)

protocol.setup: VSA memory: T role-filler pairs bound (product-binding) into one bundle, D=256

decoders.ambient: M^-1 @ bundle (only defined at square point T=D)
decoders.dual_single_shot: C^T M^+ C @ bundle then unbind (NOT the iterative dual resonator)

protocol.scoring: position match after argmax over stored fillers; 200 trials per T

honest_label.finding_1: pure degrades gracefully across the whole range (0.96 at T=16 to 0.07 at T=256) — no inversion needed at any point
honest_label.finding_2: dual single-shot does NOT beat pure in this regime (0.25 at T=16, worse at all T) — consistent with the P2 re-labeling: single-shot dual adds pinv noise without benefit; dual matters with ITERATIVE re-injection (the resonator loop of the paper), which this probe does not implement
honest_label.finding_3: ambient is only defined at the square point (the theorem itself): below it the system is over-determined, above it singular. At T=D its accuracy was ~0 in this single-shot configuration
honest_label.limitation: the iterative dual resonator (the actual P2 regime) is NOT tested here; that arm exists in the paper harness (Exp 18 VSA loop) and is the next step

verdict: P2 remains re-labeled: in single-shot memory decoding, pure wins; the dual's advantage requires the iterative regime. The square-point boundary (Exp 30) marks WHERE any decoder strategy must change.
